question: Which country has the shortest coastline in the world?
Everest is the highest mountain above sea level, but which summit is farthest from the centre of the Earth?
answer: Chimborazo, in Ecuador, thanks to the bulge at the equator

question: Christine Lagarde recently resigned from which board?
The European village of Fucking changed its name to Fugging in 2021 because tourists kept stealing its road signs. In which country?
Which is the only letter that does not appear in the name of any of the 50 US states?
Which is the only Nobel Prize that is not awarded in Stockholm?
answer: The Peace Prize, awarded in Oslo

question: It is a common trend to add edible gold leaf to high-end food and drinks. What flavour does gold add?
answer: None: it has no detectable flavour and is purely decorative

question: Who was the first woman buried in the Panthéon in Paris on her own merits?
On which day of the week are US midterm elections traditionally held?
Which drink became extremely popular because it contained quinine, a medicine against malaria?
Which is the only number in English whose letters are in alphabetical order?
The Moon is drifting away from us. By about how much a year? (Closest wins.)
answer: About 3.8 cm, roughly the speed your fingernails grow

question: In theory, how many times would you have to fold a sheet of paper for it to reach the Moon?
Which fictional character's full name is Barbara Millicent Roberts?
Luxembourg has won Eurovision five times. How many of those winners were Luxembourgish?
answer: None. Four were French and one, Vicky Leandros, Greek.

question: Which Canadian superstar won Eurovision in 1988, for Switzerland?
Which city did the Gëlle Fra visit in 2010, for the World Expo?
How many blue stripes are behind the red lion on Luxembourg's coat of arms?
Which euro coin has seven notches on its edge so that blind people can recognise it?
Which planet in our solar system has a day that is longer than its entire year?
Only three sovereign countries are completely surrounded by a single other country. Two of them are Vatican City and San Marino. What is the third?
The Negroni was born when Count Negroni asked for his Americano with what instead of soda water?
answer: Gin (as the family tells it, in Florence, around 1919)

question: Luxembourg's only official Olympic gold came in Helsinki in 1952, in the 1500 m. Who was the runner?
Kimi Antonelli recently became the youngest Formula 1 champion ever. Which team does he drive for?
Which two teams played in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final? Bonus point for the final score.
Simpsons characters have four fingers. Who has five?
Which game was nicknamed "sex in a box" when it launched in 1966?
Who was the first musician to become a billionaire solely from their music, songwriting and performances, without side businesses like make-up or fashion brands?
Which board game takes its name from the Swahili word for "Build!"?
What is the highest point in Luxembourg?
answer: The Kneiff (560 m). A 1997 GPS survey found it is 1 m higher than the Buurgplaatz, long believed to be the highest point.

question: Which Luxembourg-born runner won the 1900 Olympic marathon, only for the gold to be credited to France?
Which astronomer, born on 8 November 1656, calculated the orbit of a bright comet and correctly predicted its return?
answer: Edmond Halley. He also persuaded Newton to write the Principia, edited it and arranged its publication.

question: Mammoths were still alive when the Great Pyramid of Giza was built.
answer: True. Mammoths survived on Wrangel Island until about 2000 BC; the pyramid dates from about 2560 BC.

question: Old church windows are thicker at the bottom because glass slowly flows downwards over the centuries.
answer: False. Old panes were never perfectly flat, and glaziers put the thicker edge at the bottom.

question: There are more stars in the Milky Way than trees on Earth.
answer: False. There are about 3 trillion trees on Earth and 100 to 400 billion stars in the Milky Way.

question: Iceland has never had a McDonald's.
answer: False. Iceland had McDonald's from 1993 to 2009, and the last burger and fries are still on display.

question: Hot water can freeze faster than cold water.
answer: Neither. The "Mpemba effect" shows up in some experiments but can't be reliably reproduced.

question: In Switzerland it is illegal to keep just one guinea pig.
answer: True. Since 2008, Swiss animal welfare law says social animals like guinea pigs need company.

question: Bulls are enraged by the colour red.
answer: False. Bulls can't tell red from green; they charge at the movement of the cape.

question: Australia exports camels to Saudi Arabia.
answer: True. Australia has the world's largest herd of wild camels.

question: In the Middle Ages, educated Europeans believed the Earth was flat.
answer: False. Educated Europeans knew the Earth was round from Greek times; the myth dates from the 19th century.

question: Luxembourg has more cars than people.
answer: False. Luxembourg has about 670 cars per 1,000 residents: among the most in the EU, but fewer than one each.

question: Napoleon was once attacked by a horde of rabbits.
answer: True, as far as we know. One general's memoirs describe an 1807 rabbit hunt where tame rabbits charged at Napoleon.

question: Goldfish have a three-second memory.
answer: False. Goldfish can remember things for months.

question: Sharks are older than trees.
answer: True. Sharks appeared about 450 million years ago, trees about 385 million years ago.

question: A duck's quack doesn't echo.
answer: False. It does: acousticians at the University of Salford tested it in 2003.
